jobs.title: Public Policy & Advocacy Internship – Spring 2027 at U.S. Chamber of Commerce
jobs.description: Employer: U.S. Chamber of Commerce Expires: 11/23/2026 We are pleased to offer an outstanding and substantive internship program for the nation's best and brightest young leaders.At the U.S. Chamber of Commerce, you will obtain a hands-on, meaningful work experience designed to meet your academic and career goals. Our internships offer opportunities in research, writing, database management, policy, communications, and event preparation.During the internship, you will network with colleagues and senior executives while participating in educational and professional activities designed to enhance your experience. PROGRAM OVERVIEW:The Chamber Internship Program is a one-of-a-kind opportunity to learn at the world's largest business organization. In addition to directly supporting a team in the organization, interns have an opportunity to participate in a variety of programming that will help build professional skills and networks.Responsibilities for interns typically include research, drafting memos, content creation, and event planning and coordination. Specific responsibilities vary by department and semester.The Chamber also offers robust programming each semester to support professional development and networking for interns. These opportunities include company-wide meetings and social events, intern-exclusive discussions with senior executives such as the CEO, the Chief Policy Officer, and the President of the Foundation, as well as a resume review and interview preparation workshop.The internship is expected to run from February 1 through April 9. Interns work a part-time hybrid schedule and are expected to be in the office at least three days a week at our U.S. Chamber of Commerce headquarters in downtown Washington, D.C. Fully remote applicants will not be considered. Interns will be responsible for making their own housing accommodations if needed.This is a paid internship, and students may also receive academic credit if they meet the criteria set by their school. The hourly rate for this position is between $18.00 and $20.00 per hour. This internship is open to current college or graduate students, as well as individuals who have graduated within the past six months. DEPARTMENT MATCHINGThe Public Policy & Advocacy teams shape U.S. and global policy on critical issues including economic growth, energy, cybersecurity, employment, healthcare, and strategic advocacy. Interns will support policy research, legislative tracking, stakeholder engagement, and communications efforts that advance the Chamber’s pro-business priorities across public and private sectors.After you submit your resume, our Talent Acquisition team will review it. If your skills match what we are looking for, the relevant department will reach out for an interview.Please review the departments below closely. In the application, please indicate your top two department preferences. Cyber, Space, & National Security PolicyThe National Security Policy division advocates on behalf of the Chamber's members who have a direct stake in cybersecurity, defense, space, and supply chain security policy. Interns support the team with preparation, research, and materials for major events including the March Aerospace event and roundtables across cyber, space, and defense, as well as international trip preparation. This role is ideal for candidates with an interest in national security, technology policy, and Capitol Hill engagement. Economic PolicyThe U.S. Chamber's Economic Policy team serves as an in-house quantitative resource for member companies, state and local chambers, and policy teams across the building. Interns play a hands-on role tracking economic data releases and trends to support outlook briefings, assisting as quantitative consultants on domestic and international policy work, and exploring new applications of AI in the team's day-to-day operations. This is a great fit for candidates with a strong interest in economics, data analysis, and applied policy research. Employment PolicyThe Employment Policy team advances the Chamber's workforce, education, and labor policy priorities on behalf of American businesses. Interns take on substantive ownership across three core areas: supporting planning and execution of the Child Care Fly-In (a key grant deliverable), revamping the America Works homepage to strengthen external communications on education and workforce issues, and helping prepare members for ILO negotiations on chemical hazards and AI in the workplace. This role is ideal for candidates interested in labor policy, workforce development, and international employer advocacy. Global Energy InstituteThe U.S. Chamber's Global Energy Institute unifies energy stakeholders and policymakers behind a common strategy to ensure America's supply of fuel and power is adequate, stable, and affordable, while protecting national security and improving the environment. Interns support the team across three core areas: event logistics and stakeholder engagement for high-profile convenings, policy research across the electric generation, permitting, and international energy portfolios, and strategic communications including one-pagers, blog posts, newsletters, and briefing materials. A great fit for candidates interested in energy policy, advocacy, and the intersection of policy and communications. Government AffairsThe Government Affairs division is the Chamber's lobbying team, headquartered in Washington with regional offices across the country, championing pro-business priorities and advocating for America's free enterprise system on Capitol Hill. Interns support the team with congressional hearing preparation, drafting member briefing profiles, organizing testimony materials, tracking legislation, and supporting policy forums and Hill activities. Interns are also encouraged to attend Hill meetings and events, gaining firsthand exposure to the legislative process and the Chamber's advocacy work. Housing PolicyThe Housing Policy team leads the Chamber’s national initiative to address America’s housing shortage by advancing pro-growth policies that increase housing supply and affordability. Interns support the team across three core areas: land use and permitting reform, housing finance and capital access, and workforce and immigration policy. Responsibilities include policy research, legislative tracking, stakeholder engagement, and communications support to advance the Chamber’s housing advocacy efforts. This role is ideal for candidates interested in housing policy, economic growth, and public policy development. Chamber Technology Engagement CenterThe Chamber Technology Engagement Center (C_TEC) is at the forefront of the Chamber's work on emerging technology policy, including artificial intelligence, robotics, and quantum computing. jobs.description: Employer: Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education Expires: 11/26/2026 Application Deadline10/30/2026 3:00:00 PM Eastern Time ZoneDescription*Applications will be reviewed on a rolling-basis.USDA Forest Service Office/Lab and Location: A fellowship opportunity is available with the US Department of Agriculture (USDA) Forest Service (FS) within the Forest Service Northern Research Station (NRS) located in Grand Rapids, Minnisota.At the heart of the USDA Forest Service's mission is their purpose. Everything they do is intended to help sustain forests and grasslands for present and future generations. Why? Because their stewardship work supports nature in sustaining life. This is the purpose that drives the agency’s mission and motivates their work across the agency. It’s been there from the agency’s very beginning, and it still drives them. To advance the mission and serve their purpose, the USDA Forest Service balances the short and long-term needs of people and nature by: working in collaboration with communities and our partners; providing access to resources and experiences that promote economic, ecological, and social vitality; connecting people to the land and one another; and delivering world-class science, technology and land management.Research Project: You will focus soil and forest floor samples and their preparation for long-term, forest-productivity studies. You will experience how to collect and analyze vegetation data. Mentored by a research scientist, you will train on laboratory techniques and equipment used by a laboratory manager (chemist), a physical sciences technician, forest ecologist, and other staff. Through these interactions, you will see how and why samples are prepared for chemical analysis, and how analysis of soil and vegetation data contributes to forest ecology studies. Forest Service staff will share through discussions and hands-on training how science support careers contribute to research in government agencies and academia.Learning Objectives: Under the guidance of a mentor, you will have the opportunity to learn to:Understand how and why samples are prepared for chemical analysis and apply that knowledge.Apply laboratory techniques and equipment used to prepare samples for chemical analysis.Develop laboratory skills to research and research operations that support the mission of Forest Service Research and Development.Understand how and why measurements are made and preliminary data analysis is completed.Detail how science support careers contribute to research in government agencies and academia.Mentor: The mentor for this opportunity is Stephen Sebestyen (stephen.sebestyen@usda.gov). If you have questions about the nature of the research, please contact the mentor.Anticipated Appointment Start Date: October 2026. Start date is flexible and will depend on a variety of factors.Appointment Length: The appointment will initially be for ten months but may be extended upon recommendation of USDA Forest Service and is contingent on the availability of funds.Level of Participation: The appointment is partial participation.Citizenship Requirements: This opportunity is available to U.S. citizens only.ORISE Information: This program, administered by ORAU through its contract with the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) to manage the Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education (ORISE), was established through an interagency agreement between DOE and USDA Forest Service. Participants do not become employees of USDA, USDA Forest Service, DOE or the program administrator, and there are no employment-related benefits. Proof of health insurance is required for participation in this program. Health insurance can be obtained through ORISE.Questions: Please visit our Program Website. After reading, if you have additional questions about the application process please email ORISE.USFS.NRS@orau.org and include the reference code for this opportunity.QualificationsThe qualified candidate should be currently pursuing or have received an associate’s or bachelor’s degree in the one of the relevant fields.Stipend$680.00 – $1,360.00 MonthlyPoint of ContactMicheleEligibility RequirementsCitizenship: U.S. Citizen OnlyDegree: Associate's Degree or Bachelor's Degree.

jobs.title: William M. Lapenta NOAA Student Internship 2027 at National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA)
jobs.description: Employer: National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) Expires: 11/26/2026 OverviewNOAA is offering paid summer internships through the William M. Lapenta NOAA Student Internship Program targeted towards current 2nd and 3rd-year undergraduate and enrolled graduate students to work in areas that will provide robust research and/or operational experience that will prepare the student for further study in NOAA fields, for application to fellowships or for the NOAA-mission workforce. This internship program enables the National Weather Service, (NWS), Office of Oceanic and Atmospheric Research (OAR), National Environmental Satellite Data and Information Service (NESDIS), National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS), National Ocean Service (NOS) and Office of Marine and Aviation Operations (OMAO) to target the skills needed to fulfill their specific mission needs. Projects may be focused on research areas or the development of operational products such as decision support tools, climate and weather forecast models, population dynamics of fish populations, ecosystem modeling, hydrology, ocean circulation models, unmanned systems (both in air and under water), data analysis methodologies, social science, and strategies to communicate climate and weather information pertaining to NOAA's mission to the public and to stakeholders. Overall, students will focus on areas that will meet the future needs of NOAA’s ever-broadening user community and address immediate challenges across a diverse spectrum from the sun to the bottom of our oceans.Eligibility: Must be enrolled in an undergraduate (sophomore and junior status only) or graduate degree program (as of during the internship); if not enrolled during the internship intern will be ineligible for Direct Hire. This includes all students graduating before the internship begins. Must be a U.S. Citizen willing to undergo a security background check. US citizenship must be in hand by December 10, 2026.Students from all STEM majors and other majors relevant to NOAA's mission will be considered.How to apply:Application process is conducted via SmartSheets (https://app.smartsheetgov.com/b/form/72e9abb368834d598b275f412d81a9e3) Prepare the following to be uploaded to the site.A personal statementCurriculum Vitae (CV) or resumeA transcript (unofficial is sufficient) from your institutionTwo letters of recommendation are required to be submitted on your behalf. At least one reference must be from a professor or academic advisor. The second reference may also be an academic reference or a character reference (e.g., employer, coach) who can speak to your capabilities and interests as they relate to the internship. Please ask your references to start on letters as soon as possible. Letters of recommendation are due about a week after closeout of application portal. The letters can be sent by email to peter.roohr@noaa.gov or lapenta.internships@noaa.gov.See the Program Website for more information.

jobs.title: Residential Support Staff Internship at Homeless Solutions Inc.
jobs.description: Employer: Homeless Solutions Inc. Expires: 11/27/2026 Homeless Solutions' motto is: "A Hand UP, Not a HandOUT". As an organization, we pride ourselves in providing people in need with the tools they need to succeed. From financial education to career preparation, housing navigation assistance and childcare scholarships, mental health and addiction support, and so much more, Homeless Solutions has a vast menu of services that help our guests achieve financial self-sufficiency and housing stability, all of which would not be possible without our dedicated and compassionate staff.Our Main Shelter is staffed 24/7, 365 days a year with professionals who truly care about the well-being of our guests. With over forty years of success under our belt, we know well that the most important skill our staff members possess is a purpose for fulfilling our mission. We also know that the future of our programs lies in our ability to continuously retain and attract passionate staff members who want to help transform the lives of people experiencing homelessness.To that end, our paid internship program offers college students the unique experience of working for a robust nonprofit organization and gaining hands on experience with a multitude of subpopulations while receiving ample support and guidance from a team of some of the most experienced and knowledgeable professionals in the industry.Our Residential Support Staff Interns work front-line shifts in our Main Shelter alongside our permanent employees, during which they learn the internal operations of an emergency shelter, including specific skills, such as: drug/alcohol testing, safety checks and contraband searches, de-escalation and crisis prevention techniques, medication monitoring, volunteer engagement, emergency response procedures, conflict resolution, child welfare interventions, and more. Opportunities to learn about non-profit operations, advocacy and management career paths are also available.Our paid interns typically work 16-24 hours per week for one semester or 3-4 months at a time. Many interns are offered the opportunity to continue working for Homeless Solutions beyond their initial internship period either as regular or per-diem employees dependent upon performance, interest, and availability. Many of our former interns have since built careers at Homeless Solutions post-graduation including some who currently work as Specialists and even Division Managers.Throughout our internship program, interns will gain valuable hands-on experience by meeting directly with clients, developing proficiency in using NJHMIS, and assisting with clerical work. They will also have the opportunity to shadow case management and gain firsthand exposure to social work responsibilities. Additionally, interns will have the opportunity to benefit from direct mentorship through our Mentorship Program, where they will receive guidance and professional development from experienced higher-level staff.Opportunities for paid internships at Homeless Solutions are limited and competitive. All candidates must be fingerprinted, possess a minimum of a high school diploma or the equivalent of a high school diploma and be currently enrolled in a higher education program, and be motivated to learn.Requirements:Currently enrolled in a secondary education program in the field of social work, criminology, sociology, psychology or related field.Knowledge, skills and abilitiesGood oral, written and basic computer skills.Regular and predictable onsite attendance and reliable transportation are required during the scheduled hours for this position.Physically capable of lifting and carrying supplies, up to 30 poundsAbility to occasionally move about inside the residential housing facility, including navigating stairs and ramps.Clarity of vision at close and long range.HSI is an equal opportunity employer, and we appreciate and celebrate the diversity of our staff. jobs.title: Summer Law Clerk at Kaplan Kirsch
jobs.description: Employer: Kaplan Kirsch Expires: 11/27/2026 We are looking for highly motivated and creative law students to join our dynamic, regulatory and projects-oriented law firm as a full-time Law Clerk for Summer 2027. We are seeking law students who envision a public-interest career but may want to explore unique opportunities outside of the public sector. Founded in 2003 as an alternative to the "business of law as usual," Kaplan Kirsch is a fast-growing, collegial, and collaborative national specialized law firm. Although we are a private law firm, we pride ourselves on our significant work for public entities and in the public interest. A majority of our clients are states, local governments, Native American Tribes, airport authorities, transit agencies, renewable energy companies, and non-profit organizations. Our firm offers a rare opportunity to work on matters that shape how people and goods move, how regions grow, and how communities stay connected. Just as important, it is deeply meaningful: our clients own and operate essential public assets, including airports, rail systems, and energy infrastructure, among others. The legal work surrounding these projects affects millions of travelers, businesses, and communities across the United States every day. Our leadership includes multiple former U.S. Department of Transportation General Counsels and former chief counsels from the Federal Railroad and Federal Transit Administrations. Our firm also advises on a variety of environmental regulatory, permitting, enforcement, and conservation matters for our clients. We have extensive litigation experience across our practice areas to address disputes in court as needed. Our summer program offers Law Clerks real-world experience, substantial responsibility, and mentorship from attorneys at every level. Our Law Clerks are key members of the Firm, engaging in various types of substantive legal work on matters across the country and our practice areas. Our goal is to expose our Law Clerks to a wide variety of disciplines while gaining valuable experience, training, and insight into the legal profession. Position details: This position is available at one of the Firm’s offices in Denver, San Francisco, or New York. We expect our Summer Law Clerks to work 40 hours a week. This position will be paid an hourly rate of $50.00 per hour. The Firm can also generally accommodate requests for academic credit.
